significance.root_decision: The conjecture holds in its full range c ≥ ⌈n/2⌉. The source's Lemma 7 and Corollary 1 give b = d₂ when the two spacings and the two additivity parameters satisfy an inequality, which covers c ≥ ⌈(2n−1)/3⌉, and the authors say that their technique does not reach further. The new tool is a Run Lemma about the multiset of lengths of zero runs of the cyclic difference word of a sequence in the class B(n, c, d): comparing these run lengths before and after the shift handles the overlap that the published argument leaves open, and a reflection argument on cyclic windows finishes the proof. Lean states the source's Definitions 2 and 3 and the shift R^b literally for sequences Fin n → Bool, includes the membership of the original sequence in B(n, c, n − c) that the MathDB paraphrase leaves implicit, proves that the additivity parameter exists and is unique on the class, and proves the conjecture; it also shows by an example that the strict inequality in the hypothesis is needed.
significance.caveat: The journal version (IEEE Trans. Inform. Theory 72(8) (2026) 6189–6203, doi 10.1109/TIT.2026.3695307) could not be read: the reviewer puts 0.12 on its settling Conjecture 1 and 0.03 on the related Liang–Zeng–Tang ISIT 2026 paper doing so (0.17 that some unread or missed public work settles it), so both should be checked by hand before any unqualified novelty claim; the only arXiv version leaves the conjecture open and says the authors' technique does not prove it. The Lean statement reads the source's Definition 3 with additivity parameter t ≥ 0 (the source says positive t but uses add = 0; both readings are covered). Proof, first (same-model) review and Lean are by Claude Opus 5.5; the cross-model review and final check are by GPT-6.2 Sol (two rounds; not routine 0.72).
